definition: WholeUnlocated F := ¬Spatiotemporal.Located F F.whole. WholeAbsent o F w := ¬o.ExistsAt w F.whole. Occupant ExistenceNaturalism plus WholeUnlocated implies WholeAbsent by instantiation at the same whole. This says neither that the whole is not a part of itself nor that it cannot stand in a spatiotemporal relation.
note: Analyst scope comparison, attribution deferred. The located-whole control allows occupation of the global region, without implying an external container or presence merely by power. The unlocated-absent-whole control retains another existing located candidate. This is a relationalist-style escape at the selected interface, not a complete relationalism theory. No occupation→proper-part, physical→spatiotemporal or existing-cause→all-edges bridge is introduced; U and the whole-to-part causal bridge remain open.
